project: kcl/thttpserver — a minimal HTTP server on kklass with GNU netcat as the network backend; kcl addition with own names (THttpRequest, THttpResponse, THttpRouter, THttpRouteObject, THttpServer, THttpApplication) plus a transport seam (THttpTransport, TNetcatTransport with two pre-spawned listener slots, TReplayTransport). FPC fcl-web is a design reference only. Goal: demonstrate kklass, not a full web server.
status: IN PROGRESS — P0 done 2026-09-29 (messages + replay transport, 137 unit tests); P1 done 2026-09-29 (router, 265 unit tests); P2–P3 pending. PLAN.md written 2026-09-27, D6–D9 added and a critic pass folded in 2026-09-28 (3 blockers, 11 majors, 12 minors, nits; PLAN §8).

decisions.D1: own kcl names: kcl/thttpserver, THttp* classes; FPC fcl-web is a design reference only (recommendation was FPC-anchored kcl/fphttpserver — overruled)
decisions.D2: GNU netcat only + TReplayTransport test double
decisions.D4: AcceptIdleTimeout default 0 (off, as FPC); tests always set 1000 ms
decisions.D5: pre-spawn the next listener right after the current request line arrives, in P2; two FIFO-backed slots (bash allows one coproc); fallback to a single coproc listener if the FIFO mechanics prove unreliable on msys — owner to be told — critic 2026-09-28: feasible only with an O_WRONLY writer, the child closing the other slot's fds, a cat stdin relay and a drained close (PLAN §2.5); re-verified by the supervisor 3/3 on both bashes
decisions.D6: request fields are read-only properties over private fields (property X read _x); generalised by critic C7 to every field another object reads. Measured: a plain var of another object read directly prints and leaves RESULT unchanged (stale); a property read is silent + RESULT; a write to a read-only property is rc 1 with kklass's own stderr line
decisions.D7: RegisterRoute PATTERN METHOD HANDLER [ISDEFAULT [DATA]] (with >=3 args the 2nd is always METHOD); route object gets DATA in RouteData, function / inst.method handler as $3; stored in ${inst}_rdat (never _data)
decisions.D8: an abstract route class is refused at registration with rc 2, by reading ${CLASS}_class_abstract (the flag .new checks) — no probe instance (critic C17); roadmap note: a public kk.isAbstract in kklass
decisions.D9: THttpApplication.ServerClass (default THttpServer) so a descendant server plugs in; non-server class -> Initialize rc 2

per-request cost measured: ReadFrom of a 4-header GET from a file 3.1-3.3 ms; a 64 KiB body from a file ~80 ms, over a PIPE ~1.19 s (both bashes) — see measured_p0.pipe_body
deviations: Attach FD [ISHEAD [BANNER]]: a third optional argument + private var _banner (default 'kcl-thttpserver', '' = no Server line). §1.3 lists `Attach FD ISHEAD` only, but §2.3 requires the server's ServerBanner to be validated at send, so the response must receive it

validation failure -> 500 with the DEFAULT head: default banner and Content-Type, no custom header, empty body (Content-Length: 0); Code/CodeText/ContentType are updated to what was sent (so a later access log is truthful)
ContentSent becomes 1 on ANY write attempt, a failed one included (the server must never try a second write); SendContent before Attach is rc 1 (not 2)

SendRedirect only SETS (Code, CodeText '', Location) — FPC TResponse.SendRedirect semantics (httpdefs.pp:3047); CODE default 302, must be 300-399; URL non-empty without CR/LF; else rc 2 with nothing changed
Write joins its arguments with one space and appends verbatim, no newline
Content-Length must be plain digits within int64 (kk.isInt alone would accept '+3' and '007'); a repeated IDENTICAL Content-Length is kept once (not joined), a different one is 400

parser check order: request-line length 414 -> structure (exactly two SP, three non-empty parts) or any control character 400 -> version not HTTP/D.D 400 -> method 501 -> target not '/…' 400 -> version not 1.0/1.1 505 -> headers (431/400) -> HTTP/1.1 without Host 400 -> Transfer-Encoding 501 -> Content-Length 400/413 -> body; an empty request line is 400 (no RFC leading-CRLF skip)
header value: any control character other than HTAB is 400 (§2.2 names obs-fold only; RFC 9110 field-value), OWS trimmed on both sides
an error status leaves Method..Content empty; RemoteAddress and the headers read so far are kept
a code with no reason in the table is sent as `HTTP/1.1 299 ` (empty reason, SP kept); Content-Type is omitted when ContentType is '' and for 1xx/204; Server is omitted when the banner is ''

query: names are percent-decoded too; a NAME with %00 is skipped; a VALUE with %00 marks the name rejected (QueryField rc 1) and, being the first occurrence, a later valid one does not replace it; `?g` gives g = '' rc 0

TReplayTransport: capture path `<request file>.N.out` (N = accept ordinal, ResponseFile N); per-instance arrays `_rqf`/`_rsf`, private `_next`; Accept's RESULT = the ordinal; an Accept with a connection still open closes it first; Shutdown only closes the current connection; IDLE_MS/REQ_TIMEOUT_S ignored; AddRequestFile rc 1 for a non-regular / unreadable file; ResponseFile rc 1 for a non-integer index too
HasHeader '' is rc 2 (+ one kk.debug line), consistent with GetHeader ''
HeaderNames also refuses the `__THS_` prefix (an OUTARR named __THS_REASON would clobber the reason table)
SendContent does not (cannot, fork-free on 5.2) ignore SIGPIPE itself: the caller must — THttpServer.BeginServe does (§2.6)
fork-free proof: a 4th part (DEBUG-trap canary under set -T, positive control included) beyond PLAN §4's three; the body grep ignores `$((` (arithmetic) and `||` (not a pipe)

measured_p0.nameref_length: bash 5.2.37: `${#v}` of a kklass var (declare -n v="inst_data[v]") is 0; 5.3.9 gives the real length. Repro: class with `var _m`, body `_m=GET; kk._return "${#_m}"` -> 0 on 5.2.37, 3 on 5.3.9; `${_m:1}` and `${_m%T}` work on both. Take lengths from a local copy
measured_p0.epochrealtime_locale: EPOCHREALTIME uses the locale's decimal separator: `1790634659,903380` under LC_ALL=ru_RU.UTF-8 — the unit uses `${EPOCHREALTIME//[!0-9]/}`
measured_p0.nul_in_line: `IFS= read -r -n 8194` over `ab\0cd\n` gives `abcd` rc 0, silently (both bashes): a NUL in the request line or a header is dropped, not detectable; only a body NUL is 400
measured_p0.pipe_body: `read -d '' -n N` reads a PIPE one byte per syscall: a 65536-byte body takes ~1.19 s over a pipe vs ~80 ms from a file (both bashes) — relevant to P2's per-request model (§2.8) with MaxContentLength 65536
measured_p0.exec_group_idiom: `{ exec {fd}<missing; } 2>/dev/null` fails with rc 1, prints nothing and leaves the shell's stderr intact; no fd leak on success (fd count +2 per Accept, back to the start after CloseConnection)
measured_p0.sigpipe_exit: a write to a pipe whose reader is gone kills a bash without `trap '' PIPE` with rc 141 (preserved through `timeout`)

handler resolution once at registration: INST.METHOD = ${INST}_class set + wrapper function defined + METHOD in ${CLASS}_class_methods and NOT in ${CLASS}_class_properties (so INST.Var, INST.ComputedProp, INST.delete/.call/.property are refused); a bare name deriving from THttpRouteObject (kk._class_derives_from) with ${CLASS}_class_abstract != 1 and CLASS.new defined = class; else a defined function; else rc 2

fact 16 (router half): HEAD → HEAD/ALL route first, else the GET route of a matching pattern; on the wire (replay capture) 200 + the GET Content-Length, no body. fact 17: 37-row pattern table parsed from 003's comment block, 404/405 + Allow, registration order, defaults, the ≥3-arg METHOD rule, three kinds, property wrappers refused, route object freed after every request (3/3 ctor/dtor, no __ths_route_obj vars/functions left). fact 20: 13 DATA values (spaces, *, $(…), backticks, '', -n, =, newline, ${IFS}, backslashes, lead/trail blanks, %41&x=1) verbatim as $3 and RouteData across all three kinds. fact 21: a route class with no HandleRequest → rc 2, stdout+stderr empty, constructor counter 0

handler contract (§2.11): exactly three args REQ RESP DATA for functions / INST.METHOD, two for HandleRequest; a handler reading $req.Method/.RouteParam/.PathInfo and $resp.Code prints nothing; a handler with `local BeforeRequest AfterRequest RouteCount state …` leaves the router intact; a BARE `AfterRequest=…` in a handler writes the router's property (pinned as the documented hazard)

fork-free routing: BASHPID, PATH='' and the DEBUG-trap canary (set -T, positive control) over RouteRequest with a route object / INST.METHOD / function / 404 / 405; stored bodies of both classes contain no $( ` |
measured cost (worker probe, 50 iterations, 10 routes, match at the 10th, request already parsed): RouteRequest with a function handler ≈4.3-4.4 ms, with a route object ≈5.1-5.6 ms, both bashes
deviations: a default route ALSO matches its own pattern as an ordinary route, in registration order (FPC's FindHTTPRoute semantics); 'pattern ignored' applies to its use as the fallback, which captures no params. PLAN §2.4 can be read either way

405 wins over the defaults: when some route's pattern matches the path but not the method, the answer is 405 even if a default route exists for the method (PLAN §2.4's literal order: 'no route matches the path → default'). FPC would serve the default instead
default fallback order: the method's own default, for HEAD then the GET default, then the ALL default (C13's HEAD → GET carried over to defaults)

bare `:` (one non-empty segment, no capture) and bare `*` (the rest, no capture) are accepted; a `*` anywhere but at the start of the last segment is rc 2 (so `/a*`, `/**`, `/a/*b*` are refused, not only `*` in a middle segment). Duplicate param names: the later one wins (not refused). The PATH given to FindRoute also has its leading `/` optional

RouteRequest flow beyond PLAN §2.4's one line: BeforeRequest non-zero → the handler is skipped, AfterRequest still runs, Before's rc is returned; BeforeRequest that SENT the response → the handler is skipped (FPC RouteRequest's ContentSent safety), rc 0; AfterRequest always runs (also after 404/405 and a failing handler); rc = the first non-zero of Before/handler/After; 404/405 are rc 0 (answers — a non-zero would become 500 in the server)

rc 2 cases of RouteRequest: argument count ≠ 2, REQ/RESP not identifier-shaped or not instances of (a descendant of) THttpRequest / THttpResponse, a request whose Method is '' (not parsed), a non-empty hook that is not a handler-shaped name of a defined function (checked before anything runs; AfterRequest is re-read and re-checked after the handler), a registered function / INST.METHOD that no longer exists at dispatch (silent, kk.debug)

route objects: a live __ths_route_obj left by an aborted pass is deleted before the new one is created; a constructor failure's rc is returned and HandleRequest is not run; the object is deleted whatever HandleRequest returned
FindRoute: METHOD must be one of the 8 HTTP methods (ALL, lower case, '' → rc 2); a miss sets the global REPLY and emits one kk.debug line (kcl §1.2)

'a class that forgot override HandleRequest' (assignment wording) is read as a class that does not implement HandleRequest at all: kklass treats a redeclared `proc HandleRequest` WITHOUT `override` as an implementation (class_abstract 0) — pinned in 003 as accepted and served

measured_p1.override_not_required: class TX : TBase (TBase has `abstract proc HandleRequest`) declaring `proc HandleRequest` without `override` + a body → TX_class_abstract=0, TX_abstract_methods=(), .new rc 0 (both bashes, probe1.sh). D8 therefore only catches a MISSING HandleRequest
measured_p1.class_methods_content: ${CLASS}_class_methods lists methods incl. the destructor and kklass's synthesized `_get_X`/`_set_X` for `property X read G`, but not the constructor; plain vars and property names are in ${CLASS}_class_properties only — the INST.METHOD check relies on that split
measured_p1.local_shadows_nameref: a handler's `local P=…` shadows a caller frame's `local -n P=D[p]` without writing D; a bare `P=…` writes D[p] (both bashes, probe2.sh)

review_remarks: R1 (reviewer, 2026-09-29): route params must be percent-decoded before they reach the handler. Done: matching stays on the RAW PathInfo (an encoded %2F never splits a segment; PathInfo stays undecoded); each captured value is decoded before SetRouteParam by the new file-scope ths._decodeParams, which calls the P0 ths._decode with a new optional mode `path` (`+` stays `+`; otherwise the same loop: %XX → byte, invalid %G1 / truncated %4 literal, backslashes doubled before %b) under a local LC_ALL=C — no duplicated loop, fork-free (003 §8 canary now routes a decoded param); a *rest value is decoded as a whole (%2F → /); %00 in any captured value → Code 400, rc 0, handler (and route object) not run, Before/After still run, no param set. 003: 4 pattern-table rows changed/added (x=$(id), x=a/b, x=a+b+A%G1%4, path=a/b/c/) + the table comment, canary case, new §9 with 22 tests (%20, %C3%B6, %2F in :param, literal +, %2B, %G1, trailing %4 and %, literal backslash, %5C, %5Cn%5Cx41, \x41%41, hostile %24%28touch%20pwn%29 and %60…%60 verbatim and never executed, *rest decoding, raw /p/a/b → 404, %00 in :param and *rest → 400 with the handler not run and hooks run, 400 on the wire, route object gets the decoded value and none is created on %00). Red against the pre-R1 code: 19 FAIL of 131 in 003 (the new cases that already held — literal +, %G1, %4, %, backslash, empty rest, 404, no pwn — passed as they should). After: unit suite 290/290 (001: 53, 002: 42, 003: 131, 008: 64) on 5.2.37 threaded and single and on 5.3.9 threaded; master sweep left to the reviewer
